questions.text: What does "claimed" imply when used as a reporting verb?
questions.hint: "'Claimed' implies that this is something that might not actually happen, or might be disputed."

questions.text: According to Reading 2, what does memory do with past experience?
opts: Reconstruct it — adding the rememberer's perspective
questions.correct: Reconstruct it — adding the rememberer's perspective
questions.hint: "Memory is not a passive recorder but an active interpreter." It reconstructs, not replays.

questions.text: According to Reading 1, what is the difference between "admitted" and "said"?
questions.hint: "Admitted implies that the speaker was reluctant or that the information is somewhat uncomfortable."

questions.text: The texts argue that reported speech is only a grammatical exercise.
questions.hint: Both texts argue reported speech is "a critical literacy skill" and "carries responsibility" beyond grammar. ✅

questions.text: Omitting crucial context when reporting is a form of ___ .
questions.hint: "Omitting crucial context are all forms of MISREPRESENTATION — even if entirely unintentional."

questions.text: Daniyar reported that Kamila argued journalism "shapes opinion more than politicians." What did Kamila actually say?
opts: Journalism can sometimes be as powerful as policy — a weaker claim
questions.correct: Journalism can sometimes be as powerful as policy — a weaker claim
questions.hint: Kamila: "can sometimes be as powerful as policy." Daniyar: "shapes opinion MORE than politicians." Daniyar's version is a stronger claim.

questions.text: What convention does Prof Akhmetov describe for citing sources in academic writing?
opts: Use present tense ("Smith argues") unless work is outdated
questions.correct: Use present tense ("Smith argues") unless work is outdated
questions.hint: "When you cited someone's work, you usually used the present tense — 'Smith argues' not 'Smith argued' — unless the work was clearly outdated."

questions.text: What was the rector's announcement about the B2 requirement?
opts: It applies from 2027 intake — not current students
questions.correct: It applies from 2027 intake — not current students
questions.hint: "From the 2027 intake, students will need to demonstrate B2 English proficiency... Current students are not affected."

questions.text: What did Prof Akhmetov insist about academic writing?
opts: The point is not to report what sources say but to engage with what they mean
questions.correct: The point is not to report what sources say but to engage with what they mean
questions.hint: "The point of academic writing wasn't to report what others had said but to think about what it meant."

questions.text: What is the difference between "acknowledge" and "admit" according to the professor?
opts: "Admit" carries a stronger sense that something went wrong
questions.correct: "Admit" carries a stronger sense that something went wrong
questions.hint: "'Admit' carries a stronger sense that something went wrong."

questions.text: The student council president claimed they were not given enough time to respond. How did the rector react?
opts: Accepted it was challenging and promised improvement
questions.correct: Accepted it was challenging and promised improvement
questions.hint: "I accept that the consultation process could have been longer. We intend to improve this for future policy decisions."

questions.text: Students who fail the B2 assessment will automatically not graduate.
questions.hint: "We have no intention of withholding graduation from students who make genuine effort."

questions.text: The rector described English proficiency as a ___ professional skill.
questions.hint: "English proficiency is not an add-on — it is a CORE professional skill." ✅

questions.text: "I am studying English." → She said she ___ English.
questions.hint: PC → PPC in reported speech. "am studying" → was studying. ✅

questions.text: "I will help you." → He said he ___ help me.
questions.hint: will → would in reported speech. ✅

questions.text: "She told that she was ready." — What is wrong?
questions.hint: TELL always needs a person object. "She TOLD ME that she was ready." ✅ "Told that..." ✗

questions.text: "Where do you work?" → She asked where I ___.
questions.hint: Reported question: PS (do work → worked). Normal word order — no "did." ✅

questions.text: "Are you coming?" → She asked ___ I was coming.
questions.hint: Yes/No question → "if" or "whether." "She asked IF/WHETHER I was coming." ✅

questions.text: "Don't leave!" → He told her ___ leave.
questions.hint: tell + obj + NOT + TO + infinitive. "He told her NOT TO LEAVE." ✅

questions.text: "He suggested to go to the cinema." — What is wrong?
opts: "suggested" cannot be followed by "to + infinitive" — should be "going" or "that we go"
questions.correct: "suggested" cannot be followed by "to + infinitive" — should be "going" or "that we go"
questions.hint: suggest + GERUND or suggest THAT. NEVER "suggest to do." ✅

questions.text: "I didn't steal it." → She ___ stealing it.
questions.hint: "deny" + gerund = denied STEALING. Perfect choice for denying an accusation. ✅

questions.text: "I must finish this today." → She said she ___ finish it that day.
questions.hint: "must" (obligation) → "had to" in reported speech. "today" → "that day." ✅

questions.text: "The choice of reporting verb frames the meaning." "Frames" means:
opts: Presents in a particular way to suggest an interpretation
questions.correct: Presents in a particular way to suggest an interpretation
questions.hint: "frame" = to present something to encourage a particular reading or interpretation.

questions.text: "Memory reconstructs rather than replays." "Reconstructs" means:
opts: Builds up from parts — creates, not copies
questions.correct: Builds up from parts — creates, not copies
questions.hint: "reconstruct" = to build back up; an active process of creating meaning, not a playback.

questions.text: "She was reluctant to share the news." "Reluctant" means:
questions.hint: "reluctant" = not wanting to do something; doing it against your preference.
